subject: B
topic: Sectional revision — GK & Current Affairs India

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Cabinet Mission that came to India in 1946 was headed by:
questions.explanation: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, the Secretary of State for India, led the three-member Cabinet Mission that proposed a grouping scheme and a Constituent Assembly. 'Sir Stafford Cripps' is wrong because he was a MEMBER of this mission and had separately led the Cripps Mission of 1942. 'A. V. Alexander' is wrong because he was the third member, the First Lord of the Admiralty. 'Lord Wavell' is wrong because he was the Viceroy who hosted the mission and convened the Simla Conference, not its head.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian National Congress:

(i) It was founded in 1885 at Bombay.
(ii) Its first president was W. C. Bonnerjee.
(iii) The Surat split occurred in 1907.
(iv) The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was concluded between the Congress and the Hindu Mahasabha.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the first session met in December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay. Statement (ii) is correct — Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee presided. Statement (iii) is correct — the moderates and extremists parted ways at Surat in 1907. Statement (iv) is FALSE because the Lucknow Pact was an understanding between the Congress and the MUSLIM LEAGUE, negotiated with Tilak and Jinnah playing leading roles; every option containing (iv) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Preamble of the Constitution of India was amended for the first and only time by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 inserted the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' into the Preamble, the only occasion on which it has been altered. '44th Amendment' is wrong because the 1978 amendment undid several other changes of 1976, including the restoration of the Lok Sabha's normal term and the removal of the right to property from Part III, but it did not touch the Preamble. '24th Amendment' is wrong because it affirmed Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights. '52nd Amendment' is wrong because it added the anti-defection provisions.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the sobriquets in Column I with the cities in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Manchester of India
(b) Queen of the Arabian Sea
(c) City of Lakes
(d) Pink City

Column II:
(i) Udaipur
(ii) Jaipur
(iii) Ahmedabad
(iv) Kochi

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad's cotton mills earned it the name Manchester of India; Kochi is the Queen of the Arabian Sea; Udaipur with Pichola and Fateh Sagar is the City of Lakes; Jaipur's pink sandstone gives it the name Pink City. The option calling Kochi the Manchester of India is wrong because Kochi's fame rests on its harbour, not textiles. The option pairing Jaipur with lakes and Udaipur with pink buildings is wrong because it interchanges two Rajasthan cities. The option calling Jaipur the Manchester of India misplaces an industrial epithet.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Duncan Passage lies between which two islands?
questions.explanation: The Duncan Passage is the strait separating South Andaman from Little Andaman in the Bay of Bengal. 'Great Nicobar and Little Nicobar' is wrong because those are separated by the St George's Channel further south. 'North Andaman and Middle Andaman' is wrong because the water body between them is a narrow creek system, not the Duncan Passage. 'Car Nicobar and Great Nicobar' is wrong because the wide channel in that part of the archipelago is the Sombrero Channel.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Fundamental Rights under the Constitution of India?

(i) Right to equality before the law
(ii) Right against exploitation
(iii) Right to constitutional remedies
(iv) Right to work

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Equality before the law (Article 14), the right against exploitation (Articles 23 and 24) and the right to constitutional remedies (Article 32) are all in Part III and are enforceable in the courts. The right to work appears in Article 41 among the DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES in Part IV and is not justiciable, though it inspired statutory schemes such as MGNREGA. Hence every option containing (iv) must be rejected.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The President of India is elected indirectly.
Reason (R): The President is chosen by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct because the people do not vote directly for the President. (R) is correct because Article 54 provides for an electoral college of elected MPs and elected MLAs, with the Delhi and Puducherry assemblies included by amendment. (R) explains (A) precisely, since election by a college of representatives is what makes the process indirect. The second option is wrong because the link is definitional. The third is wrong because the composition stated is accurate. The fourth is wrong because the election is indeed indirect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The production of foodgrains in a country over four years, in million tonnes, was:

2020 → 250
2021 → 265
2022 → 280
2023 → 300

What was the percentage increase in production from 2020 to 2023?
questions.explanation: The rise is 300 - 250 = 50 million tonnes on a base of 250, so the increase is (50/250) x 100 = 20%. '16.7%' is wrong because it divides 50 by 300, using the final year rather than the base year as the denominator. '25%' is wrong because it corresponds to a rise of 62.5 million tonnes on the same base. '18%' is wrong because it would follow from a rise of 45 million tonnes, which does not match the figures given.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act of 2005 was later renamed after which leader?
questions.explanation: The Act was renamed the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act in 2009, and the scheme is universally known as MGNREGA, guaranteeing a hundred days of wage employment to a rural household. 'Jawaharlal Nehru' is wrong because his name attaches to the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission. 'Indira Gandhi' is wrong because her name is carried by the old Indira Awaas Yojana and the National Old Age Pension Scheme. 'Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel' is wrong because his name is used for the Statue of Unity and the national police academy, not this employment law.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the United Nations:

(i) Each member state has one vote in the General Assembly.
(ii) A negative vote by a permanent member on a substantive matter in the Security Council amounts to a veto.
(iii) The United Nations currently has 193 member states.
(iv) The United Nations has four official languages.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the General Assembly follows the principle of sovereign equality with one vote per state. Statement (ii) is correct — the veto applies to non-procedural questions. Statement (iii) is correct — membership stands at 193 after South Sudan joined in 2011. Statement (iv) is FALSE because the UN has SIX official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. Every option containing (iv) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which mountain pass connects Sikkim with Tibet?
questions.explanation: Nathu La, at about 4,300 metres on the old Silk Route, links Sikkim with the Chumbi valley in Tibet and was reopened for border trade in 2006. 'Shipki La' is wrong because it connects Himachal Pradesh with Tibet along the Sutlej. 'Bara Lacha La' is wrong because it lies on the Manali-Leh road within Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh. 'Rohtang Pass' is wrong because it connects the Kullu valley with Lahaul and Spiti, entirely inside Himachal Pradesh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: A form of government in which the head of state is elected rather than hereditary is called a __________.
questions.explanation: In a republic the head of state holds office by election for a fixed term, which is why the Preamble describes India as a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic. 'monarchy' is wrong because a monarch inherits the office, as in the United Kingdom. 'oligarchy' is wrong because oligarchy means rule by a small privileged group and says nothing about how the head of state is chosen. 'theocracy' is wrong because in a theocracy authority is claimed to derive from religious law or a divine mandate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Guru Shikhar is the highest peak of which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Guru Shikhar, about 1,722 metres high near Mount Abu in Rajasthan, is the highest point of the Aravalli, one of the world's oldest fold mountain systems. 'Vindhya' is wrong because the Vindhyan hills are lower and their high points lie in Madhya Pradesh. 'Satpura' is wrong because the highest peak of the Satpura is Dhupgarh near Pachmarhi. 'Western Ghats' is wrong because the Ghats rise much higher, culminating in Anai Mudi in Kerala.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the countries in Column I with their currencies in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Bhutan
(b) Iran
(c) Israel
(d) Turkey

Column II:
(i) Rial
(ii) Lira
(iii) Ngultrum
(iv) Shekel

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Bhutan uses the ngultrum, pegged to the Indian rupee; Iran uses the rial; Israel uses the shekel; Turkey uses the lira. The option giving Iran the shekel and Israel the rial is wrong because it interchanges two West Asian currencies of very different origin. The option giving Bhutan the rial is wrong because the rial belongs to Iran and to some Gulf states. The option giving Turkey the rial and Iran the lira is wrong because the lira is the Turkish unit, historically shared with Italy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: A country's merchandise exports rose from ₹20 lakh crore to ₹25 lakh crore in a year. What was the percentage growth in exports?
questions.explanation: The increase is ₹5 lakh crore on a base of ₹20 lakh crore, so the growth is (5/20) x 100 = 25%. '20%' is wrong because it divides 5 by 25, using the final figure as the base instead of the initial one. '5%' is wrong because it reports the absolute increase of 5 as if it were a percentage. '30%' is wrong because a 30% rise on ₹20 lakh crore would have produced exports of ₹26 lakh crore, not ₹25 lakh crore.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Speaker of the Lok Sabha exercises a casting vote.
Reason (R): The Speaker votes in the first instance along with all the other members of the House.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: (A) is correct because Article 100 gives the Speaker a casting vote to resolve a tie. (R) is FALSE because the Speaker does NOT vote in the first instance; that abstention is precisely what preserves the impartiality of the chair and makes the casting vote necessary. The first two options are wrong because they require (R) to be true. The fourth option is wrong because the Speaker's casting vote is a settled constitutional provision.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: At the National Film Awards, the Best Feature Film is honoured with the:
questions.explanation: The Swarna Kamal or Golden Lotus is given for the Best Feature Film and for a few other top honours at the National Film Awards. 'Silver Lotus (Rajat Kamal)' is wrong because the Rajat Kamal goes to most other categories, such as best actor, best direction in some years and regional films. 'Dadasaheb Phalke Award' is wrong because it is a lifetime achievement honour for a person, not a film. 'Indira Gandhi Award' is wrong because that National Film Award recognises the best DEBUT film of a director.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Ramsar sites in India?

(i) Chilika lake
(ii) Keoladeo National Park
(iii) Loktak lake
(iv) Jim Corbett National Park

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Chilika in Odisha and Keoladeo in Rajasthan were among India's first Ramsar sites in 1981, and Loktak in Manipur followed in 1990; all three are wetlands of international importance. Jim Corbett is a tiger reserve and national park in Uttarakhand, valued for terrestrial wildlife rather than designated as a Ramsar wetland. Hence every option containing (iv) must be rejected.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which soil type covers the largest area of India?
questions.explanation: Alluvial soils deposited by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra systems and the coastal deltas cover roughly two-fifths of the country and support its most intensive agriculture. 'Black soil' is wrong because black cotton or regur soil is confined largely to the Deccan lava region of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. 'Red soil' is wrong because red soils occupy the crystalline peninsular uplands, a smaller share. 'Laterite soil' is wrong because laterites form only in areas of heavy seasonal rainfall with alternating wet and dry spells.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about SAARC:

(i) The SAARC Charter was signed at Dhaka in 1985.
(ii) Decisions in SAARC are taken on the basis of unanimity.
(iii) Bilateral and contentious issues are excluded from SAARC deliberations.
(iv) SAARC members share a common currency for trade among themselves.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the Charter was signed at the Dhaka summit of December 1985. Statements (ii) and (iii) are correct because the Charter expressly requires unanimity in decisions and keeps bilateral and contentious matters off the agenda, which is one reason for the body's slow progress. Statement (iv) is FALSE because SAARC has no common currency; economic cooperation has advanced only to arrangements such as SAFTA. Every option containing (iv) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is remembered as the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance'?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha, campaigned against sati and for women's education, and is called the father of the Indian Renaissance and of modern India. 'Swami Vivekananda' is wrong because his work at the Chicago Parliament of Religions and with the Ramakrishna Mission came at the end of the nineteenth century. 'Dayanand Saraswati' is wrong because he founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 with a call to return to the Vedas. 'Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar' is wrong because his great contribution was widow remarriage and educational reform in Bengal, building on Roy's earlier work.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the schemes in Column I with their objectives in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana
(b) Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana
(c) Atal Pension Yojana
(d) Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

Column II:
(i) Housing for all
(ii) LPG connections for poor households
(iii) Guaranteed pension for unorganised sector workers
(iv) Improving the child sex ratio and girls' education

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Ujjwala provides subsidised LPG connections to women of poor households, Awas Yojana aims at pucca housing for all, Atal Pension Yojana gives a guaranteed pension to unorganised workers and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao addresses the child sex ratio and girls' schooling. The option swapping Ujjwala and Awas Yojana is wrong because Ujjwala is a clean-fuel scheme. The option pairing Atal Pension Yojana with the sex ratio is wrong because it is a social security scheme. The option pairing Ujjwala with pensions misplaces a household energy programme.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which gas is filled in electric bulbs to prevent the filament from burning away?
questions.explanation: Argon, often mixed with nitrogen, is a chemically inert gas that surrounds the tungsten filament, prevents oxidation and slows evaporation of the metal. 'Oxygen' is wrong because oxygen would immediately oxidise the white-hot filament and destroy it. 'Hydrogen' is wrong because hydrogen is highly inflammable and also conducts heat away rapidly, cooling the filament. 'Carbon dioxide' is wrong because although less reactive than oxygen, it can still react at filament temperatures and is a poorer choice than a noble gas.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Governor of a State is elected by the people of that State.
Reason (R): The Governor is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: (A) is FALSE because there is no popular election for a Governor; the Constituent Assembly deliberately rejected that idea. (R) is TRUE because Article 155 provides for appointment by the President by warrant under his hand and seal, and Article 156 makes the tenure subject to the President's pleasure. The first two options are wrong because they require (A) to be correct, and the third is wrong because it rejects an accurate statement of the appointment process.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Read the following data and answer the question that follows.

The sectoral shares in a country's Gross Domestic Product were:

Agriculture → 18%
Industry → 28%
Services → 54%

If the GDP was ₹200 lakh crore, what was the contribution of industry?
questions.explanation: 28% of ₹200 lakh crore is 200 x 0.28 = ₹56 lakh crore. '₹36 lakh crore' is wrong because that is 18% of the GDP, the AGRICULTURAL contribution. '₹108 lakh crore' is wrong because that is 54% of the GDP, the contribution of SERVICES. '₹28 lakh crore' is wrong because it treats the percentage figure 28 as if it were already the amount in lakh crore, forgetting to apply it to the GDP total.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India:

(i) The CAG is appointed by the President of India.
(ii) The CAG holds office for six years or until attaining the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
(iii) The CAG audits the accounts of both the Union and the States.
(iv) The CAG may be removed by the President at his own discretion at any time.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Article 148 provides for appointment by the President by warrant under his hand and seal. Statement (ii) is correct — the tenure is six years or age 65, whichever comes first. Statement (iii) is correct — the CAG audits Union and State accounts and reports to the respective legislatures. Statement (iv) is FALSE because the CAG can be removed only in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court, that is by an address of both Houses on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity; every option containing (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Bhakra Nangal project is a joint undertaking of which group of states?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra Nangal project on the Sutlej is managed by the Bhakra Beas Management Board for the partner states Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan, which share its water and power. 'Punjab, Haryana and Delhi' is wrong because Delhi receives a share of power but is not one of the original partner states of the project. 'Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand' is wrong because although the dam physically stands in Himachal Pradesh, that state is not among the partner beneficiaries. 'Rajasthan, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh' is wrong because those states are partners in the Narmada, not the Sutlej, projects.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are member countries of ASEAN?

(i) Vietnam
(ii) Myanmar
(iii) Bangladesh
(iv) Philippines

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Vietnam joined ASEAN in 1995, Myanmar in 1997 and the Philippines was a founding member in 1967. Bangladesh is a SOUTH Asian country and belongs to SAARC and BIMSTEC, not to ASEAN, whose membership is confined to South-East Asia. Hence every option containing (iii) must be rejected, and the option omitting the Philippines leaves out one of the five original signatories of the Bangkok Declaration.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first Indian to be appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: General K. M. Cariappa took over as the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army in January 1949 and was later made a Field Marshal. 'Sam Manekshaw' is wrong because he became Chief of the Army Staff in 1969 and led the army in the 1971 war. 'Rajendrasinhji Jadeja' is wrong because he was the SECOND Indian to hold the post, succeeding Cariappa in 1953. 'Roy Bucher' is wrong because General Bucher was the last BRITISH Commander-in-Chief, whom Cariappa replaced.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the events in Column I with their years in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Jallianwala Bagh massacre
(b) Beginning of the Dandi March
(c) Launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement
(d) Arrival of the Cripps Mission

Column II:
(i) 1920
(ii) 1942
(iii) 1919
(iv) 1930

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The Jallianwala Bagh firing took place on 13 April 1919; the Dandi March began on 12 March 1930; Non-Cooperation was launched at the Nagpur session and put into effect from 1920; the Cripps Mission reached India in March 1942. The option dating Jallianwala Bagh to 1920 is wrong because the Rowlatt agitation preceded Non-Cooperation. The option dating the Dandi March to 1920 is wrong because Civil Disobedience followed a decade later. The option dating Jallianwala Bagh to 1930 confuses two separate phases of the struggle.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Konkan Railway runs from Roha in Maharashtra to which terminus in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Konkan Railway's 741-km route ends at Thokur near Mangaluru in Karnataka, having crossed the Sahyadri spurs with hundreds of bridges and tunnels. 'Karwar' is wrong because Karwar is an important station on the line but not its southern terminus. 'Udupi' is wrong because Udupi too is an intermediate station on the coastal stretch. 'Hubballi' is wrong because Hubballi lies inland on the Deccan plateau and is a divisional headquarters of the South Western Railway, off the Konkan alignment altogether.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India has a parliamentary form of government.
Reason (R): India is a federal state with a written Constitution.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct because the real executive is a Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. (R) is also correct because India is a federal polity with a lengthy written Constitution. But (R) does not explain (A): federalism concerns the DIVISION of power between levels of government, while the parliamentary system concerns the RELATIONSHIP between the executive and the legislature — the United States is federal yet presidential. The third and fourth options are wrong because both statements are true.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Indian state has the largest area under forest cover?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest area in absolute terms among Indian states, thanks to its extensive teak and sal tracts on the central plateau. 'Arunachal Pradesh' is wrong because although it ranks very high and has the largest forest cover as a PERCENTAGE of geographical area among the larger states, its total area is smaller. 'Chhattisgarh' is wrong because it ranks after Madhya Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh. 'Maharashtra' is wrong because its forest area, while substantial, is smaller still than that of Chhattisgarh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the climate of India:

(i) The south-west monsoon normally reaches Kerala around 1 June.
(ii) The retreating monsoon brings rain to the Coromandel coast in October and November.
(iii) Western disturbances bring winter rain to north-western India.
(iv) The 'Loo' is a cold wind that blows across northern India in winter.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the monsoon onset over Kerala is dated around 1 June. Statement (ii) is correct — the north-east or retreating monsoon gives Tamil Nadu its main rainfall. Statement (iii) is correct — western disturbances water the rabi crop of the north-west. Statement (iv) is FALSE because the 'Loo' is a HOT, dry and dusty wind of the northern plains in May and June, not a winter wind, so every option containing (iv) fails.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In which year did the Election Commission of India become a permanently multi-member body?
questions.explanation: Two Election Commissioners were appointed alongside the Chief Election Commissioner in 1993, and the three-member structure has continued ever since. '1989' is wrong because two Commissioners were appointed in October 1989 but the posts were abolished a few months later, in January 1990. '1950' is wrong because the Commission was set up on 25 January 1950 as a single-member body. '1996' is wrong because by then the multi-member arrangement was already three years old.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The policy of integrating a country's economy with the world economy through the freer flow of trade, capital and technology is called __________.
questions.explanation: Globalisation refers specifically to opening up to the world economy through trade, investment and technology flows, and was one of the three pillars of India's 1991 reforms. 'liberalisation' is wrong because it means relaxing domestic controls such as industrial licensing, which is an internal loosening rather than external integration. 'privatisation' is wrong because it means transferring ownership from the state to private hands. 'protectionism' is wrong because it is the opposite policy, of shielding domestic industry with tariffs and quotas.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: According to the Census of 2011, which Union Territory recorded the highest literacy rate?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep recorded about 91.8% literacy in 2011, the highest among the Union Territories and second only to Kerala among all states and UTs. 'Puducherry' is wrong because its literacy was about 85.8%, high but below Lakshadweep. 'Chandigarh' is wrong because it stood at roughly 86.0%. 'Delhi' is wrong because the National Capital Territory recorded about 86.2%, again short of the island territory's figure.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are writs that the Supreme Court may issue under Article 32?

(i) Habeas corpus
(ii) Mandamus
(iii) Quo warranto
(iv) Injunction

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Article 32 names five writs — habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto — for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. An injunction is an ordinary equitable remedy granted by civil courts under procedural law and is NOT one of the constitutional writs. Hence every option containing (iv) must be rejected, and the option omitting habeas corpus leaves out the most fundamental of the five.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In a state legislative assembly of 90 seats, a party won 54 seats. What percentage of the seats did it win?
questions.explanation: The share is (54/90) x 100 = 60%. '54%' is wrong because it repeats the number of seats as though the assembly had 100 members. '65%' is wrong because 65% of 90 would be 58.5 seats, which is not a whole number and does not match the data. '58%' is wrong because 58% of 90 is about 52 seats; only 54 out of 90 reduces exactly to three-fifths, that is 60%.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the newspapers and journals in Column I with their descriptions in Column II:

Column I:
(a) The Hindu
(b) Young India
(c) Harijan
(d) Bombay Chronicle

Column II:
(i) Gandhi's weekly of the 1930s devoted to social reform
(ii) Founded in 1878 by G. Subramania Iyer and his associates
(iii) English weekly edited by Gandhi from 1919
(iv) Started by Pherozeshah Mehta with B. G. Horniman as editor

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The Hindu began in 1878 under G. Subramania Iyer and his colleagues; Young India was Gandhi's English weekly from 1919; Harijan, started in 1933, carried his campaign against untouchability; the Bombay Chronicle was founded by Pherozeshah Mehta with Horniman editing it. The option swapping Young India and Harijan is wrong because Harijan came more than a decade later with a specific social focus. The option pairing The Hindu with the Bombay Chronicle's founder is wrong because Mehta's paper was a Bombay nationalist daily. The option pairing the Chronicle with Gandhi's weekly misdates both.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Schedule of the Constitution of India contains the provisions relating to disqualification on the ground of defection?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment of 1985, sets out the anti-defection provisions under which a legislator may be disqualified for voluntarily giving up party membership or defying a party whip. 'Ninth Schedule' is wrong because it lists laws, mainly on land reform, placed beyond ordinary challenge. 'Eleventh Schedule' is wrong because it lists the 29 subjects for panchayats under the 73rd Amendment. 'Twelfth Schedule' is wrong because it lists the 18 subjects for urban local bodies under the 74th Amendment.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's foreign trade:

(i) A trade surplus arises when the value of exports exceeds that of imports.
(ii) Petroleum and crude oil are among India's largest import items by value.
(iii) Special Economic Zones are intended chiefly to promote exports.
(iv) India's single largest export item by value is raw cotton.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct by definition of a surplus. Statement (ii) is correct — crude petroleum has long headed India's import bill, along with gold and electronic goods. Statement (iii) is correct — SEZs offer duty-free enclaves with fiscal incentives to boost exports. Statement (iv) is FALSE because India's leading exports are petroleum products, engineering goods, gems and jewellery, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, while raw cotton is a comparatively minor item; every option containing (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The SI unit 'candela' is used to measure:
questions.explanation: The candela is one of the seven SI base units and measures luminous intensity, that is, the light emitted by a source in a given direction. 'Sound intensity' is wrong because sound level is expressed in decibels and intensity in watts per square metre. 'Electric current' is wrong because current is measured in amperes, another SI base unit. 'Magnetic flux' is wrong because flux is measured in webers, a derived unit.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Article 1 of the Constitution describes India as a 'Union of States' rather than a federation.
Reason (R): The Indian federation is not the outcome of an agreement among the states, and no state has the right to secede from the Union.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct because Article 1 uses the words 'Union of States'. (R) is correct because Dr Ambedkar explained in the Constituent Assembly that the phrase was chosen precisely to convey that the Union is indestructible and was not created by a compact of sovereign states. (R) therefore explains (A) directly. The second option is wrong because the drafting choice rests on that very reasoning. The third and fourth options are wrong because both statements are historically and textually accurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Chipko movement for the protection of forests began in which present-day state?
questions.explanation: Chipko began in 1973 in the Chamoli district of the Garhwal Himalaya, then part of Uttar Pradesh and now in Uttarakhand, with villagers embracing trees to stop commercial felling. 'Himachal Pradesh' is wrong because although it shares similar forest conditions, the movement did not originate there. 'Karnataka' is wrong because Karnataka's comparable campaign was Appiko in the Western Ghats during the 1980s, inspired BY Chipko. 'Rajasthan' is wrong because Rajasthan's tradition of tree protection is associated with the much earlier Bishnoi resistance at Khejarli.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are kharif crops in India?

(i) Rice
(ii) Cotton
(iii) Mustard
(iv) Groundnut

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Rice, cotton and groundnut are sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon in June and July and harvested in autumn, making them kharif crops. Mustard is a RABI crop, sown in October and November and harvested in spring, alongside wheat, gram and barley. Hence every option containing (iii) must be rejected, and the option omitting groundnut leaves out a major monsoon-sown oilseed.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Duleep Trophy in Indian domestic cricket is contested between:
questions.explanation: The Duleep Trophy, named after Duleepsinhji, has traditionally been a first-class competition between zonal sides such as North Zone, West Zone and South Zone, though selected India squads have been used in some seasons. 'State teams' is wrong because state sides contest the Ranji Trophy. 'Under-19 state teams' is wrong because the leading age-group tournament is the Cooch Behar Trophy. 'Departmental and railway teams' is wrong because such institutional sides play within the Ranji structure rather than in a separate Duleep competition.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements of everyday science:

(i) Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
(ii) Light travels faster in air than in water.
(iii) A convex lens is used to correct short-sightedness.
(iv) Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct because sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium. Statement (ii) is correct because water is optically denser, so light slows on entering it. Statement (iv) is correct — mercury is the only metal liquid at ordinary room temperature, while gallium and caesium melt only slightly above it. Statement (iii) is FALSE because short-sightedness or myopia is corrected by a CONCAVE lens; a convex lens corrects long-sightedness. Every option containing (iii) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Read the following data and answer the question that follows.

The area sown under three crops on a farm and the yield per hectare were:

Wheat → 45 hectares, 4 tonnes per hectare
Rice → 30 hectares, 3 tonnes per hectare
Maize → 25 hectares, 2 tonnes per hectare

What was the total output of the farm?
questions.explanation: The outputs are 45 x 4 = 180, 30 x 3 = 90 and 25 x 2 = 50 tonnes, giving a total of 180 + 90 + 50 = 320 tonnes. '300 tonnes' is wrong because it comes from multiplying the total area of 100 hectares by an assumed average yield of 3 tonnes, which ignores the different yields. '340 tonnes' is wrong because it adds an extra 20 tonnes through an arithmetic slip in the wheat figure. '290 tonnes' is wrong because it takes the maize yield as 1.6 tonnes per hectare rather than 2.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the languages of India:

(i) The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution at present lists 22 languages.
(ii) Hindi in the Devanagari script is the official language of the Union under Article 343.
(iii) Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 21st Constitutional Amendment.
(iv) English ceased to be an associate official language of the Union in 1965.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the Schedule listed 14 languages originally and now names 22. Statement (ii) is correct — Article 343(1) makes Hindi in Devanagari the official language of the Union. Statement (iii) is correct — the 21st Amendment of 1967 added Sindhi. Statement (iv) is FALSE because the Official Languages Act of 1963, amended in 1967, allowed English to continue indefinitely alongside Hindi, so every option containing (iv) is wrong.
